question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The evidence does not show the deadline. The nearest provision says an employee who wishes to opt out "may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute," but that is the opt-out period, not confirmed as the deadline for deciding to decline. [629/2025 §33(2)(b)] (newest, Bill, 2025-08-19; identical text in GS 621/2025, 2025-07-17, and GS 551/2024, 2024-09-03).

- If declining is the same act as opting out, the period is "six months" from the offer date. [621/2025 §33(2)(b)]
- Declining triggers compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme, approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance. [551/2024 §33(2)(c)]

Caveats: The passages are truncated before any separate decision deadline; that specific provision is missing from the evidence.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The new definition reads: "'Director-General' means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act" [494/2024 §6]. The same text appears in the newer bills [595/2025 §2; 620/2025].

- All references to "Controller"/"Rubber Controller" are replaced by "Director-General" [595/2025 §2(1)], and in other written laws or documents read as "Director-General of the Rubber Development Department" [595/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: Only the 2024 Gazette text sets out the amended s.52 definition verbatim; the 2025 GS/Bill contain identical wording per the evidence but no quoted clause text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment substitutes "sixty-three years" for "sixty-one years" in section 6(3), and replaces section 6(4) so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- The new subsection 6(4) applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [058/2026 §3].
- Identical text appears in the Bill version, 064/2026 (Bill, 2026-08-18) [058/2026 §3].

Caveats: Only the Gazette text of 058/2026 (GS, 2026-08-07) is quoted verbatim; which judges fall under the increased 63-year limit depends on the existing section 6(3), not reproduced here.
